stem: Deficiencies in the terminal complement pathway (components $C5$ through $C9$) specifically increase the risk of which type of infection?
explanation: The terminal pathway forms the membrane attack complex ($MAC$), which is uniquely required to lyse the cell walls of $Neisseria$ species.
rationale: This deficiency prevents the formation of the Membrane Attack Complex ($MAC$).

optionExplanations.A: The terminal pathway forms the membrane attack complex ($MAC$), which is uniquely required to lyse the cell walls of $Neisseria$ species.
optionExplanations.B: Fungal defense is primarily handled by T-cells and phagocytes, not the membrane attack complex of the complement system.
optionExplanations.C: While complement assists in opsonization, $C5-C9$ defects are much more specific to $Neisseria$; encapsulated bacteria are usually associated with antibody or early complement ($C3$) issues.
optionExplanations.D: Viral immunity is largely cellular; complement plays a minimal role in controlling chronic intracellular viral pathogens.
